body: could be related to the early return in ["get_available_packet_count()"](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/websocket/wsl_peer.cpp#L828) returning "0" even if there could be additional packets in the buffer and/or potentially the assert? in [`get_packet()`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/websocket/wsl_peer.cpp#L811)

Furthermore, close codes and messages via WebSocket are no longer processed when using SSL. Works fine for local testing, however, in production they are completely broken. Workaround via the OPs solution is impossible.

The problem seems to be that close frames are processed before all data frames may be processed. The close frame being received results in the ready state transitioning to CLOSING and beginning the closing handshake. 

For example, you can see in “[poll()](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/websocket/wsl_peer.cpp#L738-L752)” that at line 738, no error is returned for the last message and, if you run the MRP locally, a close frame would already be sent so when you get to line 746, the condition evaluates to true and the closing handshake begins. 

There should probably be some way to handle close frames sequentially, so that any data frames sent before a close frame are dealt with first.

I hit the TLS variant @Veradictus mentioned (close codes lost over `wss://`) and traced it to a separate cause from the `STATE_CLOSING` one above.

The server sends a close frame (code 1000, no reason, so 4 bytes) and closes the connection right away. Godot then reports `get_close_code() == -1`, going straight from `STATE_OPEN` to `STATE_CLOSED`. With `--verbose`:

```
Websocket get data error: 27, read (should be 0!): 4
Websocket (wslay) poll error: -400
```

`StreamPeerMbedTLS::get_partial_data()` ([stream_peer_mbedtls.cpp](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/modules/mbedtls/stream_peer_mbedtls.cpp)) loops over `mbedtls_ssl_read()`. The first read returns the 4 bytes of the close frame. The next read hits the closed connection and returns `ERR_CONNECTION_ERROR` (or `ERR_FILE_EOF` on close_notify) with `r_received == 4`. `WSLPeer::_wsl_recv_callback()` treats any error as a failure and drops the bytes that were already read, so wslay never sees the close frame, or any data frames that arrived in the same read. That would also explain the last message going missing over TLS.

A possible fix: when `get_partial_data()` has already received bytes before the failure, return `OK` with those bytes and report the close on the next call. Alternatively, `_wsl_recv_callback()` could hand `read` bytes to wslay before failing.

Seen on 4.5.2 and 4.7.2 (Linux) against a production `wss://` server (aiohttp behind a load balancer), in roughly every call the server ends.
